pathophysiology.summary: NICE offers adults with Graves' disease carbimazole for 12 to 18 months using either a block-and-replace or a titration regimen. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (FT4) and free triiodothyronine (FT3) are checked every 6 weeks until TSH is in range, then TSH every 3 months until antithyroid drugs stop. Full blood count and liver function are checked before starting but not monitored routinely unless agranulocytosis or liver dysfunction is suspected. Antithyroid drugs are stopped and not restarted if agranulocytosis develops. Propylthiouracil is considered in pregnancy or planned pregnancy within 6 months, after adverse reactions to carbimazole, or with a history of pancreatitis.

clinicalManagement.title: Baseline tests
actions: Check full blood count and liver function; assess pregnancy plans and contraception.

clinicalManagement.title: Start carbimazole
actions: Usual adult starting dose is 20 to 60 mg a day divided 2 to 3 times; choose titration or block-and-replace regimen.

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: TSH, FT4 and FT3 every 6 weeks until TSH is in range, then TSH every 3 months.

clinicalManagement.title: Counsel on agranulocytosis
actions: Advise to report sore throat or fever; stop and do not restart if agranulocytosis occurs.

clinicalManagement.title: Stop and follow up
actions: Lower the dose and stop after about 12 to 18 months; check TSH within 8 weeks, every 3 months for a year, then yearly.

regimens.dose: 20 to 60 mg a day (usual starting dose)
regimens.frequency: 2 or 3 times daily initially; usually a single daily dose once hormone levels are stable
regimens.duration: 12 to 18 months in Graves' disease (NICE); lowered gradually then stopped
adjustments: Dose changed according to thyroid blood tests; the source describes dose reduction once levels are stable.
Pregnancy or planning pregnancy within 6 months: consider propylthiouracil.
Liver problems: raise with the doctor before taking (no dose adjustment stated).
monitoring: TSH, FT4 and FT3 every 6 weeks until TSH in range, then TSH every 3 months.
Full blood count and liver function only if agranulocytosis or liver dysfunction is suspected.
contraindications: Agranulocytosis: stop and do not restart.

Allergy to carbimazole or thyroid medicines; previous severe pancreatitis with carbimazole; blood disorders; inability to have regular blood tests; receiving or due radioactive iodine (as listed by the NHS page).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Carbimazole for 12 to 18 months by block-and-replace or titration.
TSH, FT4, FT3 every 6 weeks until TSH is in range, then TSH every 3 months.
TSH within 8 weeks, every 3 months for a year, then yearly.
Two TSH readings below 0.1 mIU/litre at least 3 months apart plus evidence of thyroid disease or thyrotoxic symptoms.
